venue.name: Beacon Hill Park
venue.description: Beacon Hill Park is a City of Victoria park of roughly 740,000 square metres in the Fairfield neighbourhood, with natural areas, manicured flower beds and meandering footpaths. The City lists ball diamonds, sports fields, tennis and pickleball courts, lawn bowling, a picnic shelter, play equipment, washrooms, beach access and trails among its amenities. Environmentally sensitive areas within the park, including Garry oak ecosystem and the Yellow Montane Violet, are protected under local, provincial and federal law. The park is the western terminus of the Trans-Canada Highway, Mile “0”.

facility_notes.washrooms: Beacon Hill Park public washrooms, listed under Dawn to Dusk locations: 210 Bridge Way; Cook and Dallas (2 Cook Street); 156 Nursery Road.
facility_notes.lunch_space: Listed park amenities include Picnic Shelter.

restrictions: Within Beacon Hill Park, dogs must be on-leash at all times, with the exception of the leash-optional area located south of Dallas Road
Consumption of alcohol within the park is prohibited
Sale of food is not permitted in BHP

programs.name: Self-guided park visit
programs.description: Open public parkland with footpaths through both manicured and natural areas. The City page lists Accessible Features, Ball Diamond, Beach Access, Natural Area, Pickleball Court, Lawn Bowling, Picnic Shelter, Tennis Court, Water View, Horticultural Interest, Play Equipment, Sports Fields, Washrooms, Leash Optional Areas and Trails/Paths as amenities. No admission price, opening hours or group booking route is published for ordinary park use.
programs.what_children_do: Walk the footpaths between manicured flower beds and natural Garry oak areas, look out across the Strait of Juan de Fuca from the open ground, and use the play equipment and open lawns.
programs.our_note: The park is large enough that a group can spend a whole morning in one corner and never see the rest, so pick a gate and a meeting point before you set off. The three washroom blocks are far apart — Bridge Way, Cook and Dallas, and Nursery Road — and are open dawn to dusk only. The City publishes nothing at all about group visits, so nobody at the other end knows a class is coming.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms at three separate locations in the park and a picnic shelter are listed among the amenities. Nothing is published about park hours, bus parking, rain shelter or a booking route for groups.
programs.evidence: Meandering footpaths offer long strolls among manicured and natural areas and features for the whole family to enjoy.

programs.name: Park activity or event permit
programs.description: A Park Permit covers private gatherings such as picnics and birthday parties, but not public events. Activities and special events proposed for Beacon Hill Park are assessed separately by Parks Division staff using an Appropriate Activity Assessment Framework, and Council approval may be necessary. Permit fees and/or deposits apply and the applicant must carry public liability insurance of at least $2,000,000 naming the City of Victoria as an additional insured. Terms are from the City's Beacon Hill Park Activity and Event Applications information sheet dated November 2022.
programs.our_note: This is only the route if you want to reserve space or run something organised; an ordinary class walk through the park is not covered by it. Allow two months and check first whether your organisation's liability policy already covers a City park booking, because $2 million of coverage naming the City is a condition of the permit.
programs.practical_summary: Fees, deposits and an insurance certificate are required but no dollar figures are published — the application form carries the current fees. Lead time is two months for gatherings under 50 people and four months for larger events.
programs.extra_fees_note: Permit fees and/or deposits will apply. Please see application for current fees.
programs.cancellation_note: The City retains the right to cancel the event up to and including the day of the event, with or without cause or at any time during the event in an emergency, or if permit conditions are not adhered to.
programs.evidence: Smaller scale applications (less than 50 people) may be submitted two months prior to the proposed activity or event.

images.alt: A bird's eye view of Beacon Hill Park. Lush trees and green grass surround a peaceful pond.

gaps: The tracker's listed website, beaconhillpark.com, is an unofficial third-party promotional site and was not used as a source; the park is City of Victoria property and victoria.ca is the venue domain.
price: no admission or fee information is published for ordinary park use, so is_free is left null rather than assumed.
youngest age: no minimum or recommended age is published for the park or its play equipment.
capacity: no group size limit is published for ordinary park use; the 50-person figure on the permit sheet is an application-timing threshold, not a capacity.
lead time: no notice period is published for a group simply visiting the park.
lunch space: a picnic shelter is listed as an amenity but the City does not say whether it can be reserved, how many it seats, or whether it is covered.
washrooms: hours are given as dawn to dusk but no accessibility or change-table detail is published.
rain backup: unknown — no covered or indoor alternative is mentioned.
hours: the City publishes no opening or closing hours for the park itself.
bus parking: unknown — no parking information of any kind is published on the park page.
stroller and wheelchair access: the park page lists 'Accessible Features' as an amenity but does not say which features or which routes are step-free.
hosts_school_groups and hosts_daycare_groups are left null: the City site is silent about school or daycare visits rather than welcoming or excluding them.
The park page's og:image is the City's generic social card (social.png), not a photograph, so the hero was taken from the lead photo on the park page instead.
